subject: biology-1
question: A person with type AB blood has both A antigens and B antigens on their red blood cells, and neither antigen is a blend of the two. This full expression of both alleles is an example of **codominance**. Which statement correctly explains how the A and B alleles produce this pattern?

options.text: The A and B alleles are incompletely dominant over each other, producing a blended antigen.
The A and B alleles are expressed together in full in the heterozygote.
Both A and B alleles must be homozygous for the AB phenotype to appear.
The AB phenotype appears only when the O allele is also present.

explanation: Codominance means both alleles are fully expressed in a heterozygote, and that is exactly what happens when both A and B antigens appear on the red blood cells of a person with type AB blood. A describes incomplete dominance, which would blend the antigens into a single new form. C is wrong because the AB genotype is heterozygous, and D is wrong because the O allele produces no antigen at all.
